newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria spends petrol fund on schools, hospitals.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria spends petrol fund on schools, hospitals.

text.p: Nigeria is to spend 20 billion naira ($250 million) on schools and hospitals from a fund set up by to cushion the blow of fuel price rises, newspapers said on Monday.
The Guardian said 24 universities and 23 teaching hospitals would benefit. At a regional level consultants have been sent across Nigeria to identify priority targets for spending.
The fund has so far not made public accounts of what it has earned or exactly what it has spent.
Analysts' estimates for the amount available since the fund was set up in October 1994 after a four-fold fuel price hike stand at over 60 billion naira.
The fund gets 5.32 naira from every litre of petrol sold at 11.00 naira, against 1.70 naira for refineries and distribution and 1.30 naira for marketers.

Clear beneficiaries so far have been construction and pharmaceutical industries. Contracts worth 32 billion naira have been awarded for road repairs, as well as 1.5 billion naira for the supply of drugs.
